draft.title: Training and development
card: builds the skills a worker needs for the job they do now, such as learning to use a new machine or a safety procedure.
prepares a worker for future roles and wider responsibility, such as a leadership course for someone who may become a manager.
Both can raise productivity, which is the output made for each hour worked. Skilled staff often work faster and make fewer mistakes.
Both can also help a business keep good staff. Workers who see a business investing in them may be less likely to leave.
draft.remember: Training is for the job now. Development is for roles to come. Both can lift output and keep staff.

a.q: A shop pays for four cashiers to do different courses. Which course is aimed at development, not training?
opts: A course to prepare for a supervisor role
A lesson on using a new card machine
A session on the shop's refund rules
A drill on safe lifting of stock
a.why: A course that prepares a cashier for a supervisor role builds skills for a future job, which is development. The other three build skills for the job the cashier does now, so they are training.
a.clue: Which course looks ahead to a different role?

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Ballarat. She pays for a new baker, Tom, to learn the safe use of a new oven. Which describes this best?
opts: Training, because it builds a skill Tom needs in his job now
Development, because it makes Tom more skilled than before
Training, because it prepares Tom to run the bakery later
Development, because the business paid for the course
b.why: Using the new oven is a skill Tom needs in his current job, so it is training. Development is about preparing for future roles, and more skill alone does not make something development.
b.clue: Ask whether the skill is for Tom's job now or a later role.

a.best: A course to prepare for a supervisor role

b.best: Training, because it builds a skill Tom needs in his job now
